aggressive_definition: Advanced-stage prostate cancer; no stage criteria are provided in the abstract.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was also investigated by localised or advanced stage and by cancer detection method.
study_design: Pooled matched case-control analysis using four prospective cohorts and a screen-detected case-control study nested in a randomized treatment trial; food diaries were completed before diagnosis.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 1,717 prostate cancer cases in middle-aged and older UK men were pooled from four prospective cohorts with clinically detected disease (n=663), with routine data follow-up (means 6.6-13.3 years) and a case-control study with screen-detected disease (n=1054), nested in a randomised trial of prostate cancer treatments (ISCTRN 20141297). Multiple-day food diaries (records) completed by men prior to diagnosis were used to estimate intakes of 37 selected nutrients, food groups and items, including carbohydrate, fat, protein, dairy products, fish, meat, fruit and vegetables, energy, fibre, alcohol, lycopene and selenium. Cases were matched on age and diary date to at least one control within study (n=3528).
reason: The pooled analysis evaluates incident prostate cancer generally and explicitly investigates risk by localized versus advanced stage. Advanced-stage disease qualifies as an aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was calculated, using conditional logistic regression (adjusted for baseline covariates) and expressed as odds ratios in each quintile of intake (±95% confidence intervals).
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied lycopene estimate is defined in existing evidence as incident prostate cancer overall, not advanced-stage disease. The abstract supports the general endpoint but does not report this numeric estimate.
